mainTopic: Repaying loans when the coin changed: cancelled coins (רב, שמואל, רב נחמן), coins across borders for מעשר שני, and coins made heavier (רב חסדא, רב אשי)
overview: This amud deals with loans and coins whose value or status has changed. רב says that if the loan's coin was cancelled, the borrower repays with a coin in use now. שמואל says the borrower may hand over the old coin and tell the lender to spend it in מישן, where it still works. רב נחמן limits שמואל to a lender who actually plans to travel there. The גמרא defends this limit against two ברייתות about redeeming מעשר שני by explaining how strict each kingdom is about coins crossing its borders. A further contradiction about using all coins in ירושלים is settled by רבי זירא: it depends on whether the Jewish people or the nations are in power. After a short ברייתא describing the coins of ירושלים and of אברהם אבינו, רבא asks רב חסדא about a loan whose coin was later made heavier. רב חסדא says the borrower pays with the current coin. When the גמרא raises the worry of ריבית, רב אשי begins to explain that we check why prices dropped, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב: Repay with a coin that is in use now
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that when the loan's coin has been cancelled, the borrower repays with a coin that is in circulation at the time of repayment.
steps.simpleTranslation: The borrower gives the lender a coin that is in use at that time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב's ruling about a loan made in a coin that was later cancelled: the borrower must pay with a currently valid coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, what counts is a coin the lender can actually use now. A cancelled coin doesn't pay back the loan, even if it is the same coin he borrowed.

keyTerms.meaning: That 'goes out', meaning it is in circulation and accepted
At that time, meaning at the time of repayment

phrases.english: He gives him a coin
that is in circulation at that time.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹתֵן לוֹ מַטְבֵּעַ הַיּוֹצֵא בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב's ruling from just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cancelled loan coin is repaid with a coin that is currently in circulation.

steps.title: שמואל: The borrower can say 'Go spend it in מישן'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב. The borrower may repay with the cancelled coin and tell the lender to spend it in מישן, where it is still accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל says: The borrower can say to the lender, 'Go spend it in מישן.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the opposite view. The borrower may return the same old coin, because it still works somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, a coin that still works in another place has not totally lost its value. So the borrower is returning what he borrowed, and the lender's job is to take it where it can be spent.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to him; he has the right to argue this
Spend it; put it into use
מישן, a distant place where the old coin is still used

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
he can say to him,
phrases.notes: The borrower is the one talking to the lender.

phrases.english: Go spend it in Meishan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's ruling in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The borrower may repay with the cancelled coin if it is still used elsewhere.

steps.title: רב נחמן: שמואל's view applies only if the lender is going to מישן
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן limits שמואל's ruling. It only applies when the lender has a reason or plan to travel to מישן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: שמואל's statement makes sense when the lender has a way to go to מישן. But if he has no way to go there, the borrower cannot pay him this way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן narrows שמואל's rule. Telling the lender to spend the coin in מישן is only fair if he is actually headed there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a trip planned, the old coin is useless to the lender. So in that case even שמואל would agree with רב that the borrower must pay in a valid coin.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable; it makes sense
A way or road, meaning a planned trip

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Shmuel's statement is reasonable
when he has a way to go to Meishan,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the lender. Literally 'he has a road', meaning he plans to travel there.

phrases.english: but if he has no way to go there – not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִילְּתֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל's ruling applies only when the lender has a way to travel to the place where the coin is still used.
steps.whyThisMatters: This limit is what the rest of the section argues about.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the law of redeeming second tithe
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא. Cancelled coins cannot be used to redeem מעשר שני, but coins that are cancelled only locally and still good elsewhere can be, with no mention of traveling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised an objection to רב נחמן: One may not redeem מעשר שני onto coins that are not in circulation. How so? If he had coins of בר כוזיבא, coins of Jerusalem, or coins of earlier kings, he may not redeem onto them. This implies that coins of later kings, which are like the earlier kings' coins, can be used to redeem!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's limit using a ברייתא about redeeming מעשר שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only rules out coins that are dead everywhere. So coins of the current kings, cancelled here but used elsewhere, must count as valid money. The ברייתא never says this depends on the owner planning a trip, which goes against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: They redeem, moving the holiness of מעשר שני produce onto coins
Coins minted by בר כוזיבא (Bar Kokhba)
Earlier kings, whose coins are no longer used anywhere

steps.confusionAlert: The 'later kings' coins' are not fully valid coins. They are like the earlier kings' coins because they were cancelled here, but they are still used in other places. That is why they match the מישן case.

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Nachman:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְחַלְּלִין עַל הַמָּעוֹת שֶׁאֵינָם יוֹצְאוֹת.
phrases.english: One may not redeem onto coins that are not in circulation.
phrases.notes: This is about redeeming מעשר שני produce by moving its holiness onto coins.

phrases.english: How so? If he had coins
of Bar Kokhba, of Jerusalem,
or of the earlier kings –
one may not redeem onto them.
This implies that coins of later kings
that are like the earlier ones – one may redeem onto them!
phrases.notes: 'Like the earlier ones' means cancelled here, but still in use somewhere else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's limit from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that a locally cancelled coin counts only if the person is traveling to where it is used.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats a coin used elsewhere as valid for redeeming מעשר שני without any travel condition. So such a coin should count as money even for someone who is not traveling.

steps.title: רב נחמן: The ברייתא is about kingdoms that don't mind
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the ברייתא is about kingdoms that don't object to their cancelled coins being taken and spent in other places.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What case are we dealing with here? Where the kingdoms are not strict with one another.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends himself. He says the ברייתא is a different situation from שמואל's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the kingdoms don't object, the coins can freely leave and be sold to travelers, so they keep real value even here. That is why the ברייתא allows them for anyone, even someone who isn't traveling.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? This sets a source in a specific situation
Are strict or particular; they object

phrases.english: He said to him:
With what are we dealing here?

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁאֵין מַלְכִיּוֹת מַקְפִּידוֹת זוֹ עַל זוֹ.
phrases.english: Where the kingdoms are not strict with one another.
phrases.notes: They don't mind if a coin cancelled in one kingdom is taken across the border and spent where it is still good.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the ברייתא in a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that a coin used elsewhere always counts as money, with no travel condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about kingdoms that don't object. There the coin is easy to trade, so it has value everywhere.

steps.title: If the kingdoms are strict, how could the lender bring the coins to מישן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא follows up: then שמואל's case must be where the kingdoms are strict. In that case, how could the lender carry the coins to מישן at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then when שמואל spoke, it was where the kingdoms are strict with one another. How can he bring the coins there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out what רב נחמן's answer means for שמואל's case and asks a practical question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the kingdoms object to moving these coins, the coins might be taken away at the border. Then telling the lender to spend them in מישן seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: But then; this introduces what follows from the last answer

phrases.english: But then, when Shmuel said his ruling,
it was where the kingdoms are strict with one another.
How can he bring them there?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the cancelled coins. The question is how he could get them into מישן without having them taken away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what step 5's answer means for שמואל's case and asks how it works in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the lender could bring the coins to מישן if the kingdoms object to moving them.

steps.title: He can bring them with difficulty, since they don't search
steps.stepSummary: The lender can bring the coins with difficulty. The authorities don't search people, but if they find the coins, they object.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brings them with difficulty, because the authorities don't search. But if they find the coins, they object.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Bringing the coins is possible but risky, which fits רב נחמן's limit on שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there is no search, a traveler can get the coins through, so שמואל's ruling works for someone going to מישן. Since the authorities do object if they find them, no one here will easily take the coins. So a lender who isn't traveling can't use them, which is just what רב נחמן said.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן limits שמואל to a lender who is traveling to מישן. The ברייתא about מעשר שני doesn't disprove this, because it is about kingdoms that don't mind coins crossing the border. In שמואל's case, the coins can be brought across only with difficulty: no one searches, but if the coins are found, the authorities object.

phrases.english: He brings them with difficulty;
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected wording, making it 'them', meaning the coins.

phrases.english: because they do not search,
but if they find the coins, they object.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The coins can be brought with difficulty: the authorities don't search, though they object if they find them.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן's limit on שמואל stands, and the ברייתא is about a different situation.

steps.title: A ברייתא about redeeming מעשר שני on coins from a different country
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: you may not redeem מעשר שני onto ארץ ישראל coins while in בבל, even though you will later bring them up to ארץ ישראל. This seems to go against שמואל's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: You may not redeem מעשר שני onto coins of ארץ ישראל while they are in בבל, or onto coins of בבל while they are in ארץ ישראל. Coins of בבל while they are in בבל, you may redeem onto. So the ברייתא teaches that you cannot use ארץ ישראל coins while in בבל, even though in the end the person is going up there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge שמואל's idea that coins count as good money because the person can carry them to a place where they work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole point of redeeming מעשר שני is to carry the money up to ירושלים. So the person is surely going to bring these ארץ ישראל coins to ארץ ישראל, yet the ברייתא still says they don't count. This suggests that coins are judged by where they are now, not by where they will be taken, which goes against שמואל's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: redeem: move the holiness of מעשר שני produce onto coins
the second tithe, eaten or spent in ירושלים
at any rate, it teaches: pointing to the key line of a source

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְחַלְּלִין עַל מָעוֹת שֶׁל כָּאן
phrases.english: One may not redeem [מעשר שני] onto coins of here
phrases.notes: "Here" means ארץ ישראל. Redeeming means moving the holiness of the produce onto the coins.

phrases.english: while they are in Babylonia,
nor onto coins of Babylonia while they are here.
Coins of Babylonia while they are in Babylonia: one may redeem onto them.
At any rate, it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְחַלְּלִין עַל מָעוֹת שֶׁל כָּאן וְהֵן בְּבָבֶל –
phrases.english: One may not redeem onto coins of here while they are in Babylonia,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּסוֹפוֹ לְמִיסַּק לְהָתָם!
phrases.english: even though in the end he will go up there!
phrases.notes: He has to go up, because מעשר שני money must be spent in ירושלים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the problem about strict kingdoms, the גמרא brings a new source against שמואל's approach.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling, as limited by רב נחמן, that coins count as good if the person can take them where they are accepted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא rejects ארץ ישראל coins in בבל even though the person will surely bring them to ארץ ישראל. So future travel does not make coins count as good money.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about kingdoms that are strict with each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about a time when the two kingdoms are strict with each other, so the coins cannot be carried across at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? With a case where the kingdoms are strict with one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the ברייתא to a special situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the kingdoms are strict with each other, you cannot carry coins from one country to the other at all. So the coins really cannot reach ארץ ישראל, and that is why they don't count. In שמואל's case the coins can be carried, even if it is hard (step 7), so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow a source)

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
When the kingdoms are strict with one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by limiting the ברייתא to a special case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say coins are judged only by where they are now, even if they will be carried elsewhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about kingdoms so strict that the coins cannot be moved across at all, so it does not argue with שמואל.

steps.title: Then what good are בבל coins in בבל?
steps.stepSummary: If the kingdoms are that strict, בבל coins can never reach ירושלים. So how can the ברייתא allow redeeming מעשר שני on them?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, coins of בבל while they are in בבל, what are they good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer by looking at the last line of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני money is supposed to be brought to ירושלים and spent there. If the borders are closed to coins, בבל coins can never get there. So why does the ברייתא say you may redeem onto בבל coins in בבל?

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, שֶׁל בָּבֶל וְהֵן בְּבָבֶל
phrases.english: If so, coins of Babylonia while they are in Babylonia,
what are they good for?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, שֶׁל בָּבֶל וְהֵן בְּבָבֶל לְמַאי חֲזוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 9 using the last clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about kingdoms that are strict with each other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If coins can't cross the border, בבל coins can never be spent in ירושלים, so redeeming onto them should be useless.

steps.title: Use the coins to buy an animal and bring it up
steps.stepSummary: בבל coins are still useful: the person buys an animal with them in בבל and brings the animal up to ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are good for buying an animal with them and bringing it up to ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the coins themselves don't need to travel. They can be used in בבל to buy an animal that does travel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kingdoms object to moving coins, not animals. So the בבל coins can be spent locally on an animal, and the animal is brought to ירושלים. That is why the ברייתא allows redeeming onto them.

phrases.english: They are good for buying an animal with them,
and he brings it up to Jerusalem.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Coins that cannot cross the border seemed useless for מעשר שני.
steps.terutzMaskana: They can be spent locally on an animal, which is then brought to ירושלים.

steps.title: But all coins were made usable in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another ברייתא: the Sages arranged that all coins could be used in ירושלים for exactly this reason. So why can't בבל coins be used in ארץ ישראל?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: They instituted that coins should be usable in ירושלים because of this!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's rule that you can't redeem onto בבל coins while in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another ברייתא says the Sages made all coins usable in ירושלים, so people from anywhere could spend their own money there. If so, בבל coins in ארץ ישראל should be fine, which contradicts the first ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: they (the Sages) instituted, made a rule

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: They instituted
that the coins should be usable in Jerusalem
because of this!
phrases.notes: "This" means so people coming from other places can use their own coins there.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ הַמָּעוֹת יוֹצְאוֹת בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם מִפְּנֵי כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the ברייתא of step 8 and sets it against another ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's clause that you may not redeem onto בבל coins while in ארץ ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the Sages made all coins usable in ירושלים, then בבל coins should work in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רבי זירא: it depends on who is in power
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains the two ברייתות speak about different times. When the Jewish people ruled, all coins could be used in ירושלים. When other nations ruled, they did not allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: This is not difficult. Here it speaks of a time when the hand of Israel was strong over the nations of the world. There it speaks of a time when the hand of the nations of the world was strong over them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא settles the contradiction by placing each ברייתא in a different period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages' rule letting all coins be used in ירושלים only works when the Jewish people are in power and can enforce it. When other nations rule, foreign coins are not accepted there, so the first ברייתא's rule applies.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about not using coins across borders is about kingdoms strict with each other, or times when the nations rule. When the Jewish people ruled, all coins were usable in ירושלים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: It is not difficult:
Here, it is a time when the hand of Israel is strong
over the nations of the world,
there, it is a time when the hand of the nations of the world
is strong over them.
phrases.notes: Literally "over themselves," but it means over the Jewish people. The גמרא says it gently.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to argue about whether בבל coins can be used in ארץ ישראל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Sages' rule works only when the Jewish people rule. When the nations rule, foreign coins can't be used.

steps.title: What the coins of ירושלים and of אברהם אבינו looked like
steps.stepSummary: Since it mentioned coins in ירושלים, the גמרא brings a ברייתא describing the coin of ירושלים and the coin of אברהם אבינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: What is the coin of ירושלים? דוד and שלמה on one side, and 'ירושלים the holy city' on the other side. And what is the coin of אברהם אבינו? An old man and an old woman on one side, and a young man and a young woman on the other side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps away from the argument and brings a side ברייתא about famous old coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not part of the back-and-forth. It is a related teaching, triggered by talk of coins in ירושלים, telling us what was pictured or written on each side of two historic coins.

keyTerms.meaning: an old man and an old woman
a young man and a young woman

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ מַטְבֵּעַ שֶׁל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם?
phrases.english: The Sages taught: What is the coin of Jerusalem?
David and Solomon on one side,
and 'Jerusalem the holy city' on the other side.
And what is the coin of Abraham our forefather?
An old man and an old woman on one side,
and a young man and a young woman on the other side.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ מַטְבֵּעַ שֶׁל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching connected to the mention of coins in ירושלים in steps 12 and 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The coin of ירושלים showed דוד and שלמה on one side and ירושלים the holy city on the other. The coin of אברהם אבינו showed an old man and old woman on one side and a young man and young woman on the other.

steps.title: רבא asks: a loan of coins, and the coin was made bigger
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב חסדא what the law is when someone lends coins and the government then makes that coin heavier.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב חסדא: If someone lends his friend money to be paid back in a certain coin, and then the government made that coin bigger, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about coins. רבא wants to know how a loan is repaid after the coin itself has changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loan was made in a coin with a fixed name, such as one זוז. Now a coin with that same name is heavier and worth more. רבא asks whether the borrower must pay with the new, bigger coin, or whether he can pay back what the old coin was worth.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a real question, looking for information)
A coin, or a type of coin
And they added to it (the coin was made heavier)

phrases.english: Rava asked of Rav Chisda:
One who lends his friend on a coin,
phrases.notes: He means the loan was set in a specific coin, to be paid back in that coin.

phrases.english: and they added to it, what is the law?
phrases.notes: "They" is the government. They made the coin heavier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: a loan repaid after the coin was made heavier. This is different from the cancelled-coin case of steps 1-3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When a loan was made in a coin that later became heavier, which coin does the borrower repay with?

steps.title: רב חסדא: pay with the coin in use at payment time
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that the borrower pays with the coin that is in use when he repays.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He gives him the coin that is in use at that time.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers רבא's question. The borrower repays with the current coin, the new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going by רב חסדא, the loan follows the coin's name, not its old weight. Whatever coin carries that name at payment time is what the borrower owes.

keyTerms.meaning: That is in use (literally, 'that goes out' in the market)
At that time, when the payment is made

phrases.english: He said to him: He gives him the coin
that is in use at that time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: נוֹתֵן לוֹ מַטְבֵּעַ הַיּוֹצֵא בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The borrower repays with the coin in use at payment time, even though it is now heavier.

steps.title: Even if the coin grew huge? Yes
steps.stepSummary: רבא tests רב חסדא's rule with extreme cases, and רב חסדא says it still applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Even if the coin became as big as a sieve? He said: Yes. Even if it became as big as a quarter-קב measure? He said: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא checks how far רב חסדא's rule goes by naming bigger and bigger changes to the coin. Each time רב חסדא answers yes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are exaggerations, meant to say 'even if the coin changed a huge amount.' רב חסדא holds his ground: no matter how big the change, the borrower pays with the current coin. This firm position sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A sieve (a way of saying 'very big')

phrases.english: He said to him: And even if it is like a sieve?
phrases.notes: רבא is asking: even if the coin grew as big as a sieve?

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.
He said to him: Even if it is like a quarter-kav?
He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far רב חסדא's answer reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rule still apply when the coin changes by a huge amount?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, even then the borrower pays with the current coin.

steps.title: But produce has become cheaper
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a bigger coin buys more produce, so the lender gets back more than he lent.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the produce has become cheaper!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's rule. If the lender gets the new, bigger coin, he can now buy more with it than he could before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the coin is heavier, the same coin buys more produce, so prices look lower. The lender receives more value than he lent, and getting back extra on a loan looks like ריבית.
steps.confusionAlert: Nothing happened to the produce itself. It only seems cheaper because the coin is now worth more.

phrases.english: But the produce is becoming cheaper!
phrases.notes: The worry is that the lender gains extra value, which looks like ריבית.

steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that the borrower always pays with the current coin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The new coin buys more, so the lender gets more value than he lent. That is a form of ריבית.

steps.title: רב אשי: check why prices dropped
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says we check the cause. If prices dropped because of the coin change, we reduce the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We look into it. If the produce got cheaper because of the coin, we reduce the debt for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי starts to answer the challenge by saying we must look at why prices fell. The rest of his answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the drop in prices comes from the heavier coin, then the lender would really be gaining extra, so the borrower may pay less to match the old value. This keeps the lender from getting ריבית. The other half of his answer, about prices that fell for another reason, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: We reduce (we take off part of the debt)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule applies whenever a currency changes in value: the repayment is fixed so that no one gains extra from the change itself.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: We look into it;
if it became cheaper because of the coin –
we reduce it for him,
phrases.notes: We take off part of the borrower's debt so he pays back only what the loan was really worth.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on the cause of the price drop
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Paying with the new coin always gives the lender extra, which is ריבית.
steps.terutzMaskana: We check the cause. If the coin change caused prices to drop, the debt is reduced so the lender gets no extra.
